requirements.evidence: app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:16-39 trims/validates the name, derives or slugifies the slug, defaults is_active to true and converts the unique-index race to ValidationException; app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:20-67 supports nullable name/slug/isActive, keeps the queue's own slug and catches the DB race; app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:23-115 authorizes, validates the permission enum, enforces the same-entity rule, upserts/revokes and logs only real revokes; app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:21-76 implements create/update/manageAccess/call, including corrupted non-array permissions; app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32 and app/Models/Ticket.php:93-121 enforce call after the active check and before the status check; database/migrations/2026_10_29_120000_create_queue_access_table.php:12-29, docs/business-rules.md:103, docs/database-schema.md:5 and CHANGELOG.md:21 complete the contract. No queue delete action exists.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes are Actions that authorize through Gate (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:18, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:27, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:29); authorization lives in App\Policies\QueuePolicy (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:16); the migration follows the generated stub and has a reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_120000_create_queue_access_table.php:12-29); QueueAccess declares its fillable fields deliberately (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:16); business rules, schema and CHANGELOG are updated in the same change; audit logging uses the audit channel (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:58,82).

security.evidence: Every action authorizes before writing (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:18, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:27, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:29); input is validated with Validator/Str (app/Actions/Concerns/NormalizesQueueAttributes.php:17-55, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:103-115); QueueAccess mass assignment is explicitly limited (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:16); QueuePolicy::call rejects non-array/corrupted permissions and non-employees (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:46-66); both call paths authorize (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32, app/Models/Ticket.php:115); no Blade/UI, unescaped output, client-controlled IDs or secrets were added.

tests.evidence: New suites cover the requirements: tests/Feature/Queue/CreateQueueTest.php:14-146, UpdateQueueTest.php:19-184, SetQueueAccessTest.php:31-162, QueuePolicyTest.php:16-106, QueueAccessModelTest.php:12-54 and CallAuthorizationTest.php:37-141, plus tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:20 (manager callers) and tests/Pest.php:60-79 (helpers). They include validation, authorization, race, corrupted-permission, inactive-order and audit cases; the one gap is the vacuous empty-permission policy test at QueuePolicyTest.php:70 (see issues).

simplicity.evidence: Name/slug normalization and slug-conflict handling are shared once via app/Actions/Concerns/NormalizesQueueAttributes.php:11-75 instead of duplicated in both actions; actions reuse Gate, Validator and Str and the existing Queue model; there is no service/repository layer. QueueAccessFactory only adds the forMembership()/forQueue() states used by the tests (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:35-50).

readability.evidence: Use-case classes, methods and test names are clear; the policy, actions and trait are documented (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:12-15, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:16-19, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:19-22); comments explain the lock order and the corrupted-permission decision (app/Models/Ticket.php:80-92, app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:63-66); no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: All changes serve the queue lifecycle/access/authorization task: new actions, model, enum, policy, migration and factory; the two call paths; the three required docs/CHANGELOG updates; and their tests. The only extra edit is the lock-order comment in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:39-41, which documents this change. No queue deletion or UI was added.

issues.explanation: The `permissions => []` grant is created with `QueueAccess::factory()->forMembership($membership)` but no `queue_id`, so it belongs to a different queue in the same entity; the assertion passes because `$queue` has no grant at all, leaving the 'array without call' denial path untested. Pass `['queue_id' => $queue->id, 'permissions' => []]` so the test actually exercises the empty-permission case.

Slug-conflict detection depends on driver-specific error-message substrings; catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException (available in this Laravel version) would be a leaner, driver-independent check and would not fall back to a raw QueryException if a driver formats its message differently.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle, the queue_access model/migration/factory, SetQueueAccess with audit logging, and a QueuePolicy enforced by both call paths, with the required docs and extensive tests. Requirements, security and conventions are met; the main finding is a policy test that does not attach its empty-permission grant to the queue under test, so that denial path is effectively untested. That is a one-line test fix, hence approve with nits.
